ai.summary: Cosmological hydrodynamical simulations model how dark matter and complex baryonic physics—such as star formation and feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN)—shape galaxies and cosmic structure, but their high computational cost and differing subgrid prescriptions make simulation-based inference and cross-code comparison challenging. To address this, the authors introduce Celia (Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions), a self-supervised foundation model using a Set Transformer and spatial attention that maps subhalo catalogs into fixed-length embedding vectors without requiring simulation parameter labels during pretraining on the CAMELS suites (IllustrisTNG, SIMBA, Astrid, and N-body). The compressed catalog embeddings provide a unified coordinate system where simple linear readouts accurately reconstruct cosmological parameters ($\Omega_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\sigma_8$) and baryonic feedback strengths, separating physical cosmological signals from cosmic variance. Crucially, the frozen encoder transfers out-of-distribution to an unseen hydrodynamics code (Swift-EAGLE) in zero- and few-shot regimes, demonstrating a viable pathway toward reusable, code-agnostic ML surrogates and simulation-based inference pipelines for galaxy surveys.

papers.title: The Conditional CMB Visibility of High-Redshift X-Ray Cavities in Galaxy clusters
papers.authors: Ramananda Santra, Samik Mitra
papers.abstract: At high redshift, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) both cools relativistic leptons and provides seed photons for inverse-Compton (IC) X-ray emission. These two effects link the particle content of a bubble directly to the soft X-ray depression used to identify a cavity. We derive a physical criterion connecting lepton cooling, bubble volume, enthalpy evolution, and 0.5--2 keV X-ray visibility, while separating intrinsic filling of the X-ray depression from detector-dependent cavity recovery. For uncooled electron populations described by a power law with spectral index $s=2.5$, minimum Lorentz factor $100\leq\gamma_{\min}\leq1000$, and maximum Lorentz factor $\gamma_{\max}=10^5$, the measured atmosphere of the testbed high-redshift cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537 requires 0.6--1.2\% of the pressure in radiating leptons to fill the soft-band deficit. Across the full tested ranges of $s$, $\gamma_{\min}$, and atmospheric properties, the required fraction is 0.2--3.7\%. Complete loss of this component reduces the enthalpy by less than 3\% relative to an otherwise identical adiabatic bubble at the same pressure. A low-cutoff control with $\gamma_{\min}=10$ and $s=3$ instead requires 18.9\%, identifying the poorly constrained low-energy spectrum as the main physical uncertainty. For a fixed atmosphere and spectrum, the required fraction scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$. The declining-pressure tracks show that the X-ray deficit can cross the adopted detection threshold while the enthalpy deficit remains below 0.4\%; the time of this transition depends on the assumed pressure history. Thus, high-redshift cavity visibility depends on both the surrounding atmosphere and the pressure-carrying particle spectrum. This criterion provides the physical basis for an instrument-specific recovery analysis.

conclusions: In the $z=1.16$ cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537, relativistic leptons need to carry only 0.6–1.2% of the total bubble pressure (for a power-law index $s=2.5$ and low-energy cutoff $100 \le \gamma_{\min} \le 1000$)—or 0.2–3.7% across the full tested range of spectra and atmospheric uncertainties—to completely fill in the 0.5–2 keV X-ray cavity deficit via IC/CMB emission.

Even if this radiating lepton component loses all of its energy to cooling, the bubble's total mechanical enthalpy ($H = 4pV$) drops by less than 3% relative to an adiabatic bubble, meaning a cavity can remain energetically powerful while becoming completely invisible as an X-ray depression.

The main physical uncertainty is the low-energy cutoff of the electron spectrum: lowering $\gamma_{\min}$ to 10 with a steep slope ($s=3$) places most of the lepton pressure in electrons too low-energy to upscatter CMB photons into the soft X-ray band, raising the required pressure fraction for fill-in to 18.9%.

For a fixed cluster atmosphere and lepton spectrum, the radiating pressure fraction required to erase the X-ray cavity scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$, making IC fill-in a rapidly growing selection effect for high-redshift AGN feedback surveys.
ai.summary: In galaxy clusters, jets from central supermassive black holes inflate relativistic plasma bubbles that push aside the hot intracluster gas; observers usually measure the mechanical energy of this "AGN feedback" by spotting the resulting dark depressions ("X-ray cavities") in soft X-ray images. At high redshift ($z \gtrsim 1$), however, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) energy density is much higher, scaling as $(1+z)^4$, so relativistic electrons and positrons inside the bubble rapidly inverse-Compton (IC) scatter CMB photons directly into the observed 0.5–2 keV X-ray band. The authors build an analytical model that couples radiative lepton cooling, bubble volume and enthalpy ($4pV$) evolution, and soft X-ray surface-brightness contrast, testing it against the measured atmosphere of the $z=1.16$ cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537. They show that a tiny fraction of bubble pressure carried by relativistic leptons can produce enough IC X-ray glow to completely fill in and hide the thermal X-ray depression without noticeably reducing the bubble's mechanical energy. This means high-redshift X-ray cavity surveys can miss mechanically important AGN bubbles simply because their own CMB-boosted IC emission masks the cavity shadow.

papers.title: Analytic Gravitational Wave Spectrum in Next-to-Minimal Bouncing Cosmology
papers.authors: Changhong Li
papers.abstract: Bouncing cosmology offers a singularity-free alternative to inflation. However, its minimal realization, known as minimal bouncing cosmology (MBC), comprises only four cosmic phases and produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a single power-law spectrum. Interpreting the pulsar timing array (PTA) signal within this framework faces tension with the $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ bound and has required trans-Planckian bounce energies, restricting its observational viability. In this work, we propose next-to-minimal bouncing cosmology (NMBC) by adding an earlier phase of cosmic evolution to MBC. Using our previously developed primordial gravitational-wave propagation-matrix method, with an improved matching prescription, we derive explicit analytic expressions for the resulting SGWB spectrum. The spectrum takes a broken power-law form: the low- and high-frequency tilts are determined by the equations of state of the additional and original contraction phases, respectively, while the spectral amplitudes depend jointly on these equations of state and the characteristic transition-time scales. This additional freedom allows a PTA-band signal to coexist with a scale-invariant or red-tilted high-frequency branch, providing a way to satisfy the $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ bound. For the scale-invariant high-frequency branch, a pointwise benchmark using the adopted $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ radiation budget gives $\rho_{s\downarrow}^{1/4}\lesssim2.65\,m_{\rm pl}$, where $m_{\rm pl}$ is the reduced Planck mass. This provides a conservative comparison estimate for the setup considered here, since integrating the spectrum over the adopted illustrative frequency interval gives a tighter bound. The resulting upper limit is therefore of order the reduced Planck scale. please refer to the PDF for the full abstract.

papers.title: Closing the Mass Window for Stupendously Large Black Holes
papers.authors: Christopher Gerlach, Yann Gouttenoire, Antonio J. Iovino, Nicholas Leister
papers.abstract: We show that primordial black holes (PBHs) in the $\textit{Stupendously Large Black Hole}$ mass range ($M \gtrsim 10^{11}\,M_\odot$) produce isocurvature perturbations exceeding current $\textit{Planck}$ Cosmic Microwave Background limits, thereby excluding them as a significant dark matter component.

papers.title: From the Solar System to cosmological distances: a complete formalism for gravitational wave astrometry
papers.authors: Gabriele Perna, Nicola Bellomo, Vincenzo Roatti, Daniele Bertacca
papers.abstract: The presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) can be established not only via exquisitely precise pulsar timing array (PTA) measurements, but also via astrometric observations. Indeed, the very same background responsible for the delay in the arrival time of pulse causes an apparent displacement of galactic objects as stars and asteroids. In this work we provide a framework that allows to derive the displacement of sources overcoming the usually adopted ``infinite distance'' approximation. We also present how this formalism can be used to study the displacements of objects at distances comparable to the GW wavelength, as asteroids, and of objects with a non-trivial three-dimensional distribution, as stars in the Milky Way. Thus, it can be used to probe frequencies beyond PTA experiments, reaching the mHz GWs, also detectable by LISA. We forecast the capability of observing the astrometric deflection induced by a GWB evaluating the harmonic signal-to-noise ratio including correlations between different probes. We find an SNR greater than one for the relevant cases considered and as a consequence a promising Fisher forecast, suggesting a constraining power up to the percent level for a flat background.

papers.title: Simultaneous determination of Hubble constant and cosmic baryon density: Forecasts for the synergy between FRBs and emerging probes
papers.authors: Peng-Ju Wu, Bo-Yang Zhang, Ji-Guo Zhang, Guo-Hong Du, Shang-Jie Jin, Xin Zhang
papers.abstract: Two of the most pressing challenges in cosmology are the persistent discrepancy in measurements of the Hubble constant, referred to as the Hubble tension, and the deficit of baryons in the local Universe, known as the missing baryon problem. Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of both the Hubble constant $H_0$ and the cosmic baryon density $\Omega_{\rm b}$. However, constraints from FRBs alone suffer from a severe $H_0$-$\Omega_{\rm b}$ degeneracy that prevents them from resolving either problem. We show that this degeneracy can be broken by combining FRBs with other emerging probes whose degeneracy directions differ in the $H_0$-$\Omega_{\rm b}$ plane. Specifically, we quantify three multi-messenger approaches: FRBs paired with gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens, strong gravitational lensing (SGL) time delays, and 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) surveys. The combinations FRB+GW, FRB+SGL, and FRB+21 cm IM each deliver simultaneous constraints on $H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}$ better than (1%, 1.5%) in the $\Lambda$CDM model, and when dynamical dark energy is introduced, the constraining precision degrades gracefully as model complexity increases. Furthermore, within a model-independent framework, both FRB+GW and FRB+SGL constrain $H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}$ to precisions better than (1.5%, 3%). These precision levels are based on nominal observational expectations and would improve significantly under optimistic observational scenarios.

papers.title: Diffusive dark fluids with Planck-2018 and DESI BAO DR2 Measurements
papers.authors: Shambel Sahlu, Amare Abebe
papers.abstract: In this paper, we constrain the diffusive dark fluid cosmological model, wherein energy is transferred between the two dark components through a diffusion process. We extended the work in Ref. \cite{sahlu2026observational} by employing Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data from the Planck 2018 measurements in combination with Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 (2024). From the results, we found that the discrepancies in \(H_0\) measurements are \(1.90\sigma\) and \(1.72\sigma\) between the Planck 2018 value \((H_0 = 67.4\pm0.5\ \mathrm{km,s^{-1},Mpc^{-1}})\) and our diffusive model values, \(H_0 = 67.27^{+0.54}_{-0.55}\;,\) and \(68.35^{+0.31}_{-0.29} \), respectively. We also observe that the effects of the interaction on cosmic evolution and structure formation; we emphasize this by computing the scale-dependent density contrast and the matter power spectrum, compared with the $\Lambda$CDM model.

papers.title: Probing non-Gaussianity during reheating with SIGW in the LISA band
papers.authors: Gabriele Perna, Guillem Domènech
papers.abstract: We analyse the effects of a non-standard evolution of the Universe during the reheating epoch on the spectrum of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) accounting for the presence of primordial non-Gaussianity. We show that given values of $w$ and $c_s^2$ leave characteristic features in the spectrum which can be detectable by third generation interferometers like LISA. In addition, we argue that the specific reheating dynamics can suppress or even enhance the spectrum, with crucial consequences for its detectability. We perform a Fisher forecast for different values of $w$ and different scans to assess the detectability of the signal when different values of the amplitude and central frequency are considered.

papers.title: Synergy between CSST and future gravitational-wave detectors: Probing primordial black holes by cross-correlating dark sirens with galaxies
papers.authors: Ya-Nan Du, Ji-Yu Song, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) events and galaxies both trace the cosmic matter distribution, but the mergers of astrophysical black holes and primordial black holes (PBHs) are expected to populate different environments and therefore to cluster with different biases. The GW clustering bias is thus a statistical observable that can separate the two populations. We assess how well this can be done by cross-correlating the photometric galaxy survey of the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) with mock GW catalogs from two future detector networks: the third-generation ET2CE network (the Einstein Telescope and two Cosmic Explorer detectors) and the multi-band BDET2CE network, which adds the space-based baseline Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory. We find that CSST combined with 10 years of ET2CE observations can reveal a PBH contribution once its fraction in the total merger rate exceeds about $40\%$, while the much sharper sky localization of BDET2CE lowers this threshold to about $20\%$. The improvement comes from recovering the small-scale clustering information that localization errors would otherwise erase. These results show that combining future GW detector networks with CSST galaxy clustering offers a promising and largely independent route to identifying PBHs statistically.

papers.title: Consistency test of the large-scale structure with Bernardeau-Nishimichi-Taruya transform of the KiDS-Legacy survey
papers.authors: Shiming Gu, Ziang Yan, Ludovic van Waerbeke, Francis Bernardeau, Hendrik Hildebrandt, Angus H. Wright, Maciej Bilicki, Christos Georgiou, Shun-Sheng Li, Laila Linke, Lauro Moscardini, Robert Reischke, Benjamin Stölzner
papers.abstract: We perform the first $k$-cut cosmic shear analysis of the KiDS-Legacy survey. This method uses the Bernardeau-Nishimichi-Taruya (BNT) transform to construct weak-lensing kernels that are more localised than conventional ones, and remove information from selected physical scales while retaining the constraining power of the targeted range. Removing the scale of $k \geq 0.33~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ from the KiDS-Legacy pseudo-$C_\ell$ data vector, and using a covariance matrix whose Gaussian component is computed from the theoretical data vector, we find $S_8 = 0.798_{-0.045}^{+0.045}$. This agrees with both the fiducial KiDS-Legacy bandpower result and our no-$k$-cut pseudo-$C_\ell$ posterior to within $0.1\sigma$, indicating no significant bias from nonlinear astrophysical feedback at the precision of KiDS-Legacy. We also study the case in which the Gaussian covariance is computed from the observed data vector. In this setup, the same scale cut of $k < 0.33~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ gives a much lower $S_8=0.717_{-0.046}^{+0.047}$. Further $k$-cut tests reveal a mild scale-dependent trend, with larger physical scales preferring lower $S_8$ values and a maximum low- versus high-$k$ deviation of $1.80\sigma$. Mock tests show that this behaviour is not produced by the covariance prescription or data vector alone, but may arise from their interplay. These results show that BNT $k$-cuts provide both a mitigation strategy for nonlinear systematics and a diagnostic of weak-lensing inference pipelines.

papers.title: photo-3x2-pt: Cosmology from cosmic shear and galaxy clustering with a single photometric galaxy catalog
papers.authors: Takashi Hamana (NAOJ)
papers.abstract: We perform a joint cosmological analysis using angular power spectra of galaxy clustering, galaxy-shear cross correlation, and cosmic shear (hereafter referred to as photo-3x2-pt) measured from the Hyper Suprime-Cam year-3 (HSC-Y3) weak lensing shape catalog. We employ the pseudo-$C_\ell$ method to measure these power spectra and use the template deprojection method to mitigate systematics in the galaxy density maps. We perform a standard Bayesian likelihood analysis for cosmological inference based on the measured photo-3x2-pt, including contributions from intrinsic alignments of galaxies, galaxy clustering bias, lensing magnification effect, baryonic feedback effect, and source redshift distribution errors. For a flat cold dark matter model, we find a 68% credible interval of $0.76 \le S_8 \le 0.81$. This result is consistent with the HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses (Dalal et al. 2023, Li et al. 2023) but is $\sim 25$% tighter. We also find that the measured B-mode power spectra are consistent with zero. We also perform a performance test using mock catalogs that mimic the HSC-Y3 data to validate our photo-3x2-pt analysis. Through Bayesian parameter inference of mock data, we verify that unbiased estimates can be obtained for the key cosmological and nuisance parameters, including $S_8$, intrinsic alignment model parameters, galaxy clustering bias, and shift parameters of the source redshift distributions.

papers.title: Conformally Coupled Scalar- Field Dark Energy: Cosmological Dynamics with Early- and Late- Measurements
papers.authors: Shambel Sahlu, Abunie Gezahegn, Amare Abebe, Gonzalo J. Olmo, Diego Rubiera-Garcia
papers.abstract:
In this work, the cosmology of the conformal interacting dark energy model is investigated by introducing a scalar field representing dark energy (DE) coupled to dark matter (DM) via a conformal transformation. This coupling yields a class of scalar+tensor theories; the interaction term ${Q}$, which indicates the flow of energy between the dark sectors, is proportional to the trace of the energy-momentum tensor of the DM fluid, $T^{\mathrm{DM}}_{\mu
u}$, as ${Q}= rac{C'(\phi)}{2C(\phi)}g^{\mu
u}T^{\mathrm{DM}}_{\mu
u}$, where $C(\phi)$ is the conformal function of a scalar potential (coupling) field. We assume the power-law parametrization $C(\phi)\propto (1+\phi)^m$, with $m$ as the coupling parameter, and determine the direction and magnitude of energy flow between the DM and DE scalar-field components. We model DE in three scenarios: conformally interacting dark energy (CIDE) coupled to a scalar field, uncoupled scalar+field DE (UCSFDE), and standard $ \Lambda$CDM models. We confront these models with cosmological measurements to test the viability of CIDE and UCSFED against $\Lambda$CDM and constrain them using a combination of early and late time data, namely: Cosmic Microwave Background measurements from Planck 2018 Legacy (	exttt{CMB}); Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Survey (	exttt{ DESI DR2 DR2 BAO}); and Supernova Type Ia distance compilations (	exttt{PantheonPlus, PantheonPlus + SH0ES, Union3}, and 	exttt{DES+Dovekie}). We perform parameter inference with Monte Carlo Markov Chain (	exttt{MCMC}) simulations using 	exttt{COBAYA} and a modified 	exttt{CLASS} ...

papers.title: Tangled $τ$: Planck CMB Constraints on Flash Reionization
papers.authors: Param Upadhyay, Elisa G. M. Ferreira, Evan McDonough
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological tensions have renewed interest in the role of reionization in parameter inference, and flash reionization has been proposed as a transient high-redshift ionization episode that can increase the Thomson optical depth while remaining compatible with CMB polarization data. In this work, we present the first Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis of the flash reionization model fit to Planck cosmic microwave background temperature, polarization, and lensing data. We perform this analysis using Planck PR4 data in $\Lambda$CDM with flash reionization. We find that CMB data allow a wide range for the redshift of the flash, $z_{\rm flash}$, but with constraints that are tightly correlated with the peak ionization fraction $x_{\rm flash}$. We find constraints $x_{\rm flash}=0.24 ^{+0.13} _{-0.07}$ and $x_{\rm flash}= 0.15 ^{+0.07} _{ - 0.05}$ for the benchmark flash reionization scenarios with fixed $z_{\rm flash}=20$ and $25$ respectively. The standard $\Lambda$CDM parameters do not exhibit any significant shifts, and in particular, the total optical depth to reionization is not appreciably changed, with $\tau=0.061 \pm 0.007$ in flash reionization as compared to $\tau=0.059\pm 0.006$ in the standard tanh parametrization. We repeat this analysis for Planck PR3 data in place of PR4, and find that the mild preference for a flash is replaced by 95% CL upper bounds, given by $x_{\rm flash}<0.28$ and $x_{\rm flash}<0.18$ for $z_{\rm flash}=20$ and $25$, respectively, from Planck PR3 data.

papers.title: Cosmic Birefringence from Large Lepton Asymmetry
papers.authors: Kentaro Kasai, Ippei Obata
papers.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the polarization plane of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons, provides an intriguing probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. In this paper, we investigate a vector Chern-Simons coupling between the neutrino current and photons as a possible origin of isotropic cosmic birefringence. Firstly, we perform the first analysis of anisotropic cosmic birefringence induced by the neutrino current. We find that the anisotropic signal sourced by lepton-number isocurvature fluctuations can be important on large scales, whereas on small scales, the anisotropic signal induced by gravitational effects becomes dominant comparing with the axion-like particle (ALP) scenario. Secondly, we show that a large lepton asymmetry generated through the Affleck-Dine mechanism can successfully account for the observed isotropic birefringence, and discuss its possible connection to the recently reported low helium-4 abundances in Subaru EMPRESS and Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT).

papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics
papers.authors: TDCOSMO Collaboration, Simon Birrer, Michele Cappellari, Frédéric Courbin, Christopher D. Fassnacht, Pierre Fleury, Joshua A. Frieman, Aymeric Galan, Xiang-Yu Huang, Daniel P. Johnson, Sanjana Khanolkar, Shawn Knabel, Hrvoje Krizic, Martin Millon, Takahiro Morishita, Veronica Motta, Pritom Mozumdar, Eric Paic, Hadrien Paugnat, Allan G. Schweinfurth, Anowar J. Shajib, William Sheu, Dominique Sluse, Massimo Stiavelli, Sherry H. Suyu, Tommaso Treu, Felipe Urcelay, Devon M. Williams, Kenneth C. Wong
papers.abstract: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $\Lambda$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $\Lambda$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_{\phi}$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5\sigma$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_{\phi}$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.

papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: new insights on the Hubble tension from strong lensing time delays
papers.authors: TDCOSMO Collaboration, Simon Birrer, Michele Cappellari, Frédéric Courbin, Christopher D. Fassnacht, Pierre Fleury, Joshua A. Frieman, Aymeric Galan, Xiang-Yu Huang, Daniel P. Johnson, Sanjana Khanolkar, Shawn Knabel, Hrvoje Krizic, Martin Millon, Takahiro Morishita, Veronica Motta, Pritom Mozumdar, Eric Paic, Hadrien Paugnat, Allan G. Schweinfurth, Anowar J. Shajib, William Sheu, Dominique Sluse, Massimo Stiavelli, Sherry H. Suyu, Tommaso Treu, Felipe Urcelay, Devon M. Williams, Kenneth C. Wong
papers.abstract: We discuss the measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) in flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter cosmology based on the blind hierarchical analysis of 11 multiply-imaged quasars (hereafter the TDCOSMO-2026 sample) and described in greater detail in a companion paper. In addition to the time delays, we use lens models based on high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), analyzed jointly with axisymmetric dynamical models based on JWST-NIRSpec, VLT-MUSE, and Keck-KCWI spectroscopy. Our primary result $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$ is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with $\Omega_{\rm m}$ constraints from the DES-Dovekie supernova (SN) dataset. Our 3% precision accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. Importantly, our measurement is independent of the local distance ladder (LDL). Among individual late-universe probes, only the traditional LDL is more precise. We discuss our result in the context of the Hubble tension, the difference between $H_0$ measured in the late universe and the prediction based on early-universe probes such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We construct combinations of independent late-universe probes and show that the tension with the Planck CMB prediction is robust to excluding any one of the methods based on Type-Ia Supernovae, Cepheids, or the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. For example, we construct a 'no-SN' $H_0$ measurement, by replacing the DES-Dovekie constraint on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ with that from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, and then combining TDCOSMO-2026 with independent non-SN late-universe probes. This 'no-SN' late-universe probe is in 3.7$\sigma$ tension with Planck. Even after completely excluding the LDL, the tension with Planck persists at the 2.7$\sigma$ level.

papers.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
papers.authors: Haotian Dong, Marek Biesiada, Zhoujian Cao, Shao-Jiang Wang
papers.abstract: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $\Lambda$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8\sigma$ to $3.9\sigma$ in the forward check and from $7.3\sigma$ to $4.3\sigma$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while the residual discrepancy is further cut in half by volumetric bias down to $\sim1.7\sigma$. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.

papers.title: Multi-Generational Black Hole Population Analysis with an Astrophysically Informed Mass Function
papers.authors: Yannick Ulrich, Djuna Croon, Jeremy Sakstein, Samuel McDermott
papers.abstract: We analyze the population statistics of black holes in the LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA GWTC-3 catalog using a parametric mass function derived from simulations of massive stars experiencing pulsational pair-instability supernovae (PPISN). Our formalism enables us to separate the black hole mass function into sub-populations corresponding to mergers between objects formed via different astrophysical pathways, allowing us to infer the properties of black holes formed from stellar collapse and black holes formed via prior mergers separately. Applying this formalism, we find that this model fits the data better than the powerlaw+peak model with Bayes factor $ 9.7\pm0.1$. We measure the location of the lower edge of the upper black hole mass gap to be $M_{\rm BHMG}=84.05_{-12.88}^{+17.19}{\rm M}_{\odot}$, providing evidence that the $35{\rm M}_{\odot}$ Gaussian peak detected in the data using other models is not associated with the PPISN pile-up predicted to precede this gap. Incorporating spin, we find that the normalized spins of stellar remnant black holes are close to zero while those of higher generation black holes tend to larger values. All of these results are in accordance with the predictions of stellar structure theory and black hole merger scenarios. Finally, we combine our mass function with the spectral siren method for measuring the Hubble constant to find $H_0=36.19_{-10.91}^{17.50}$ km/s/Mpc and discuss potential explanations of this low value. Our results demonstrate how astrophysically-informed mass functions can facilitate the interpretation of gravitational wave catalog data to provide information about black hole formation and cosmology. Future data releases will improve the precision of our measurements.

papers.title: Probing Axion-Photon Mixing with High-Resolution X-ray Spectroscopy
papers.authors: Yu Zhou, Jiejia Liu, Volodymyr Takhistov, Kazuhisa Mitsuda
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) provide a compelling avenue for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model. In astrophysical magnetized plasmas an ALP-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma}$ induces energy-dependent oscillations in the photon survival probability that imprint modulations on emission spectra. X-ray observations of bright spectrally-smooth sources can provide particularly sensitive probes of ultralight ALPs with masses $m_a \lesssim 10^{-11}$ eV due to long propagation distances, strong magnetic fields and high photon statistics. We present a comprehensive forecast of ALP-photon conversion in three representative systems: (i) background active galactic nuclei (AGNs) observed through foreground intracluster magnetic fields, (ii) central AGNs within their host cluster halos and (iii) Galactic X-ray binaries viewed through the Milky Way field. Using detailed simulations we assess the prospective sensitivity of high-resolution X-ray missions including XRISM, Athena, and Arcus. For typical magnetic field configurations a 320 ks XRISM observation or an 8 ks Athena observation of the Perseus Cluster AGN NGC 1275 can reach down to $g_{a\gamma} \sim 5 \times 10^{-13}$ GeV$^{-1}$ at $m_a \lesssim 10^{-12}$ eV, surpassing the current best limit. We quantify the impact of magnetic field modeling, photon statistics, and spectral binning strategies. Our results demonstrate the scientific potential of future X-ray observatories to probe photon-ALP coupling in previously inaccessible parameter space, offering a powerful window into physics beyond the Standard Model.

papers.title: Supernova cooling from neutrino-devouring dark matter
papers.authors: Yugen Lin, Chih-Ting Lu, Ningqiang Song
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides a powerful probe of physics beyond the Standard Model (SM), in particular for new, light states interacting feebly with SM particles. In this \textit{Letter}, we investigate for the first time the production of fermionic dark matter (DM) via the neutrino-devouring process inside a core-collapse supernova, which contributes to the excessive cooling of the supernova. By incorporating state-of-the-art supernova simulation data and the full time evolution information, we derive stringent and robust limits on DM interactions, which can improve upon direct detection limits by several orders of magnitude. We exclude the cross sections down to $10^{-51}-10^{-58}$~cm$^2$ in the keV-MeV mass range for DM-electron scattering, and $10^{-49}-10^{-56}$~cm$^2$ in the 0.1-100~MeV mass range for DM-nucleon scattering, supplemented by complementary constraints from cosmology, astrophysics, colliders and direct detection experiments in the larger cross section regime. We also close almost the entire window in which fermionic DM constitutes $\mathcal{O}(1)$ fraction of DM due to its coupling to electrons in the keV-MeV mass range.

papers.title: False Alarm Rates in Detecting Gravitational Wave Lensing from Astrophysical Coincidences: Insights with Model-Independent Technique GLANCE
papers.authors: Aniruddha Chakraborty, Suvodip Mukherjee
papers.abstract: Lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) due to intervening massive astrophysical systems between the source and the observer is an inevitable consequence of the general theory of relativity, which can produce multiple GW events with overlapping sky localization error. However, the confirmed detection of such a unique astrophysical phenomenon is challenging due to several sources of contamination, ranging from detector noise to astrophysical uncertainties. Robust model-independent search techniques that can mitigate noise contamination have been developed in the past. In this study, we explore the astrophysical uncertainty associated with incorrectly classifying a pair of unlensed GW events as a lensed pair and the associated false alarm rate (FAR) depending on the GW source properties. To understand the effect of unlensed astrophysical GW sources in producing false lensing detections, we perform a model-independent test using the pipeline GLANCE on a simulated population of merging binary black holes (BBHs). We find that $\sim$ 0.01\% of the pair of events can be falsely classified as lensed with a lensing threshold signal-to-noise ratio of 1.5, appearing at a time delay between the pair of events of $\sim$ 1000 days or more. We show the FAR distribution for the parameter space of the GW source masses, delay time, and lensing magnification parameter over which the model-independent technique GLANCE can confidently detect lensed GW pair with the current LIGO detector sensitivity. In the future, this technique will be useful in understanding the lensing FAR for next-generation GW detectors, which can observe more GW sources.

papers.title: Probing Extragalactic Ultralight Axion Dark Matter with Decade-Long Blazar Optical Polarimetry of 1ES 1959+650
papers.authors: Qiu-Ju Huang, Bao Wang, Jun-Jie Wei, Xue-Feng Wu
papers.abstract: Axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) are well-motivated dark matter (DM) candidates whose coupling to photons induces periodic oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light. This work reports the first search for such a signature using 10 years of optical polarimetric monitoring of the blazar 1ES~1959+650. No statistically significant periodicity is detected, determined by a Lomb-Scargle periodogram combined with Monte Carlo analysis. Assuming a central DM density in the host galaxy, this null result places tight upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling constant at $g_{a\gamma}<(1.3\times10^{-13}-6.0\times10^{-10})\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ across a broad ALP mass range of $m_a \sim (1.4\times10^{-23}-5.2\times10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$. Assuming a soliton-core DM density, we obtain upper limits of $ g_{a\gamma}< (2.5\times10^{-13}-6.2\times10^{-13})\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1} $ over the same ALP mass range. Our constraints surpass those from Very Long Baseline Array polarimetry of active galactic jets and from polarimetric data of the European Pulsar Timing Array, and are competitive with those from long-term Galactic pulsar timing of PSR J0437-4715 over the same ALP mass window. These results establish long-term blazar polarimetry as a competitive and complementary approach for probing axion-like DM on extragalactic scales.

papers.title: Dark Matter Interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande Antineutrino Excess and Predictions for JUNO
papers.authors: Alessandro Granelli, Silvia Pascoli, Salvador Rosauro-Alcaraz
papers.abstract: Super-Kamiokande has reported a small excess of electron antineutrino events in the 20 MeV energy range, in the search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background. We interpret this signal as a possible indication of dark matter that annihilates dominantly into neutrinos, pointing to a thermal dark matter candidate with $s$-wave annihilation and with mass in the tens of MeV range. This mass scale naturally fits into rich dark sector extensions of the Standard Model. Neutrino experiments, including JUNO, will be able to test this hypothesis in the coming years.

papers.title: LIGO, LISA and Ultralight Axion-like Dark Matter
papers.authors: Lawrence M. Krauss (The Origins Project Foundation)
papers.abstract: Interferometric searches for axion-like dark matter (ALP DM) via the induced photon birefringence in a coherent background have been proposed and analyzed by several authors over the past decade, with tabletop experiments (LIDA, ADBC, DANCE) reporting first results and detailed calculations available for both ground-based (LIGO, GEO600 via DarkGEO) and space-based (LISA, TianQin, Taiji, BBO via Gué et al. and Yao et al.) gravitational-wave detectors. We revisit this class of measurements within the framework of Krauss (2019), and provide a detailed treatment of the interplay between the DM coherence length $\lambda_{\rm coh}$, the interferometer arm length $L$, and the detector transfer function, with attention to the distinct suppression regimes $\lambda_{\rm coh} > L$ (cancellation) and $\lambda_{\rm coh} < L$ (random walk). For LIGO the sensitivity is set by the Fabry-Pérot arm cavity response peaking sharply near the cavity free spectral range, reproducing the results of Nagano et al.; the naive single-pass estimate substantially overstates the reach and cannot be applied directly. For LISA, with the polarization-sensitive modification proposed by Gué et al. or Yao et al., the natural mass range $m_a \sim 4\times10^{-19}$--$4\times10^{-16}$ eV (LISA science band) is accessible and the projected reach $g_{a\gamma\gamma}\lesssim {\rm few}\times 10^{-13}$ GeV$^{-1}$ (realistic optical-metrology noise) improves on the CAST bound over most of the band by up to about two orders of magnitude. We discuss directional signatures from the Galactic DM wind, both annual and sidereal, as a discrimination tool for candidate signals. Local DM substructure with anisotropic velocity dispersion can shift and enhance the reach in specific mass windows.

papers.title: pop-cosmos: Galaxy size evolution across structural and star-formation classifications in COSMOS-Web
papers.authors: Madalina N. Tudorache, Hiranya V. Peiris, Stephen Thorp, Sinan Deger, Daniel J. Mortlock, Gurjeet Jagwani, Anik Halder, Boris Leistedt, Benedict Van den Bussche, Joel Leja
papers.abstract: Galaxy sizes are correlated with stellar mass and redshift, as characterised by size scaling relations. The inferred forms of these scaling relations are sensitive to how galaxies are classified -- either by their star formation activity (e.g. specific star-formation rate, sSFR) or by their morphology markers (e.g. bulge-to-total ratio, Sérsic index). We combine stellar mass and sSFR estimates from pop-cosmos (a generative model trained on COSMOS2020 Spitzer IRAC $\textit{Ch.1} <26$) with size and morphology measurements from COSMOS-Web, obtaining $99,369$ galaxies. By investigating the size-mass and the size-redshift relations, we show that: (i) the sSFR/morphology splits give quantitatively different slopes, intercepts, and intrinsic scatter behaviour; (ii) intrinsic scatter depends on structural morphology but not on sSFR, which constrains the galaxy-halo connection; (iii) the quiescent and bulge-dominated size-mass relations both show double-power law breaks, but at different pivot masses, indicating that quenching and structural transformation occur on different time-scales; (iv) the morphology-dependent trends are only recoverable from space-based imaging. Further, the quiescent pivot mass $M_{\ast} \sim 10^{10.7}~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ coincides with the mass scale at which active galactic nuclei (AGN, infrared torus) bolometric luminosity fraction peaks in transitioning galaxies, while the bulge-dominated pivot mass $M_{\ast} \sim 10^{11.1}~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ coincides with the halo mass at which AGN-driven baryonic redistribution peaks, which may trace the interval over which AGN feedback ramps from quenching onset to structural transformation.

papers.title: Wave Optics Effects from Gravitational Wave Propagation Through Dark Matter Halos
papers.authors: Annamalai P. Shanmugaraj, Roland Haas, Erik Schnetter, Sofie Marie Koksbang
papers.abstract: Gravitational wave (GW) propagation is usually studied under the geometric optics approximation. However, when GWs propagate through structures of sizes similar to their wavelength, this approximation breaks down. To study this situation, we present a scheme for numerically evolving linearised plane GWs through stationary, spherical astrophysical structures in both weak and strong gravity regimes. Our simulations evolve the full Einstein equations (with all 10 components) for Gaussian, NFW and Burkert potentials. Our simulations show that the scattering of the GWs depends not only on the mass of the lens but also strongly on the gravitational potential distribution of the lens. Among our most important results, we find that the GWs do not propagate along null geodesics when propagating through the Gaussian density, neither in the strong nor weak gravity setting. Another significant finding is that in the strong gravity case of the Burkert potential, the convexity of the wave is flipped when leaving the structure. We compare our results with the linearized scalar wave predictions and find that the difference between these and the exact GW modes are of order one when the wave is inside the central potential. However, the difference reduces to only a few percent when the wave has passed through the structure. Although these effects are small, future GW detectors and Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) could be sensitive to these signals which could thus potentially help in constraining the structure of dark matter spikes or halos.

papers.title: No evidence of vorticity production from irrotational turbulent gravitational collapse yet
papers.authors: Axel Brandenburg, Evangelia Ntormousi, Jennifer Schober
papers.abstract: Gravitational collapse creates large amounts of kinetic energy that could potentially seed turbulence. If such turbulence were also suitable to initiate dynamo action, the resulting magnetic field would further modify the dynamics, especially on small length scales. However, a small-scale dynamo is believed to require vortical turbulence, whereas the collapse produces mainly irrotational motions, which may not be efficient for dynamo action. Here, we study the efficiency of vorticity production during a turbulent collapse. We adopt a barotropic equation of state, where pressure and density gradients are parallel, and no magnetic field, so that vorticity can only be produced by viscosity and by vortex dynamo-type amplification. Using direct numerical simulations of gravitational collapse, we show that, for the parameter space accessible to our numerical resolution, these effects are related to the initial irrotational turbulence and are not induced by the collapse. Vorticity production along with the associated small-scale dynamo action are still expected to occur for sufficiently large Reynolds numbers, especially when baroclinic effects are allowed for, but some of the earlier numerical evidence in the literature using a barotropic equation of state is now found to be the result of subgrid scale modeling and not reproduced in direct numerical simulations.

papers.title: Theoretical Aspects of Direct Waves in Kerr Black Holes: Pole-Splitting Method for Ringdown Analysis
papers.authors: Nao Nakamoto, Naritaka Oshita, Hiroki Takeda
papers.abstract: We develop a theoretical description of direct waves (DWs) from a particle plunging into a Kerr black hole in the extreme-mass-ratio regime. A DW is characterized by a source-driven complex frequency $\omega_{\rm G}$ that reflects the particle's orbital motion, including motion inside the ergoregion. Hence, it is expected to be a probe of rich structures of Kerr black holes. We show that the contribution of the quasinormal-mode (QNM) pole sector to the DW is part of dynamical QNM excitation. We also show that the apparent horizon-mode poles cancel at every order of a consistent near-horizon expansion of the trajectory, homogeneous radial solution, and complete point-particle source. This result assumes that the point particle follows a geodesic near the horizon and leaves open the possibility of a transient DW while the particle passes near the ergosurface or the vicinity of the potential barrier. To investigate this possibility in simulated plunge waveforms, we develop a pole-splitting method that decomposes the transfer function into QNM-pole and non-pole parts. The resulting waveform decomposition avoids the frequency-dependent time shift (group delay) introduced by the QNM filtering. For quasi-circular plunges into moderately and rapidly rotating Kerr black holes, the frequency and decay rate of the non-pole waveform show qualitative agreement with our theoretical prediction over finite time intervals. These results support the potential use of DWs as probes of the ergoregion and gravitational redshift effect around black holes.

papers.title: Dark matter haloes from dwarf to massive galaxies: no systematic inner-density tension with ΛCDM hydrodynamical simulations
papers.authors: Pavel E. Mancera Piña, Justin I. Read, Jorge Sarrato-Alós, Claudia Muni
papers.abstract: Two of the most prominent small-scale challenges to the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm are the cusp-core and diversity-of-rotation-curves problems. The former concerns the shallow inner DM density profiles inferred for many galaxies compared with the cusps predicted by collisionless CDM, while the latter concerns the wider range of inner DM densities and rotation curve shapes inferred observationally than hydrodynamical simulations traditionally reproduce. Robust observational constraints on DM core sizes and halo densities are therefore essential for testing both the nature of DM and the impact of galaxy formation processes. We analyse the inner DM distribution of a curated sample of 48 gas-rich galaxies and 8 Milky Way gas-poor satellites, spanning 6 orders of magnitude in $M_\ast$. We find substantial scatter in DM core sizes and degrees of coreness, with both cuspy and cored haloes occurring over a broad $M_\ast$ range. The cores are energetically consistent with stellar feedback, requiring modest supernova energy coupling efficiencies of order $0.1-1\%$. Comparisons with the NIHAO, FIRE-2, and EDGE simulations reveal broad agreement in the inner DM densities and logarithmic slopes of observed and simulated galaxies. The main residual differences concern the steep slopes of some massive simulated galaxies and differences in SHMRs. Using a rotation-curve diversity diagnostic from previous work, we find that extreme discrepancies with simulations are absent from our curated sample and largely attributable to uncertain kinematics or baryonic mass distributions. Within the scope of our analysis, we find no evidence of a systematic inner-density tension between our galaxy sample and current $\Lambda$CDM hydrodynamical simulations. Together with the modest energetic requirements for core formation, this substantially alleviates the cusp-core and diversity-of-rotation-curves problems.

papers.title: Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo: Accurate modeling of out-of-equilibrium decaying cosmological relics
papers.authors: Kensuke Akita, Miguel Escudero, Oleksii Ihnatenko, Maksym Ovchynnikov
papers.abstract:
We consider nonstandard cosmologies in which decaying relics inject energy at MeV temperatures, driving neutrinos out of equilibrium. The subsequent neutrino evolution shapes predictions for the cosmic radiation density and primordial light element abundances. Earlier work introduced Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo ($
u$DSMC), which describes neutrino transport through Monte Carlo sampling of particle interactions. Here, we extend this method by jointly evolving the relic population, neutrino spectra, electromagnetic plasma, and cosmic expansion, and coupling this evolution to Big Bang nucleosynthesis. The framework includes direct and inverse decays of the relic, neutrino flavor conversion, quantum statistics, and pion production by energetic neutrinos. To reveal the physical impact of these effects and independently test $
u$DSMC, we compare several approaches to neutrino evolution across a range of nonstandard cosmological scenarios. We find excellent agreement with independent solutions of quantum kinetic or quasi-classical Boltzmann equations. Compared with these calculations, $
u$DSMC includes a broader range of physical processes and is substantially faster for strongly nonthermal neutrino populations. This makes broad, robust parameter scans for nonstandard cosmologies practical. We show that when departures from thermal equilibrium are large, approximations that average over neutrino momenta can give qualitatively incorrect predictions, including the wrong sign of the change in the effective number of neutrino species and substantially incorrect primordial nuclear abundances. We conclude that the extended $
u$DSMC framework enables reliable cosmological tests of new physics by following neutrino thermalization and its observable consequences.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.authors: Tanmay Vachaspati, Anja Wachowitz
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.
